'''William Thomas Silfvast''' is an American [[physicist]] well known for his contributions to [[gas laser|gas discharge laser]]s,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Silfvast | first1=W. T. | last2=Klein | first2=M. B. | title=CW laser action on 24 visible wavelengths in Se II | journal=Applied Physics Letters | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=17 | issue=9 | year=1970 | issn=0003-6951 | doi=10.1063/1.1653453 | pages=400–403}}</ref><ref name=TLO>[[F. J. Duarte]], ''Tunable Laser Optics'' (Elsevier-Academic, New York, 2003).</ref>  soft [[x-ray laser]]s,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Silfvast | first1=W. T. |first2=M. C. |last2=Richardson|first3=H. |last3=Bender|first4= A. |last4=Hanzo|first5=V. |last5=Yanovsky|first6=F. |last6=Jin|first7=J. |last7=Thorpe| title=Laser-produced plasmas for soft x-ray projection lithography | journal=Journal of Vacuum Science & Technology B: Microelectronics and Nanometer Structures | publisher=American Vacuum Society | volume=10 | issue=6 | year=1992 | issn=0734-211X | doi=10.1116/1.585942 | pages=3126–3134| bibcode=1992JVSTB..10.3126S | s2cid=120737144 | url=https://stars.library.ucf.edu/facultybib1990/3090 | url-access=subscription }}</ref> and as the author of the influential textbook ''Laser Fundamentals''.<ref>W. T. Silfvast, ''Laser Fundamentals'' (Cambridge University, Cambridge, 2004).</ref> and also several thriller novels (see billsilfvast.com). Silfvast received his PhD in physics from the [[University of Utah]] and a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of Oxford. He then spent much of his career at [[Bell Laboratories]] in Holmdel, New Jersey, with a Guggenheim Fellowship at Stanford in 1982–83.  Later he became a professor and chairman of the Physics Department at the [[University of Central Florida]]'s Center for Research in Electro-Optics and Lasers (CREOL).  Silfvast remains a Professor Emeritus at UCF, and is now retired and living in Oregon.  He is a [[OSA Fellow|Fellow of the Optical Society of America]], the American Physical Society, and the IEEE.<ref>{{cite web|title=APS Fellowship 1993|url=http://update.aps.org:8080/units/dls/fellowship/index.cfm?year=1993|website=American Physical Society|access-date=21 May 2017}}</ref>  In 2010 Silfvast was selected as one of 27 'Laser Luminaries' (laser pioneers) during the celebration of the 50th Anniversary of the discovery of the laser.
